exposure: Pregnancy status (recently pregnant, ever pregnant, never pregnant)
Use of continuous subcutaneous insulin infusion (CSII)
outcome: Use of continuous subcutaneous insulin infusion (CSII)
cohort: The study included 4340 T1D Exchange clinic registry participants (mean age 28 ± 9 years, 84% white non-Hispanic, median T1D duration 13 years) categorized by pregnancy status as recently pregnant (n=214), ever pregnant (n=1540), or never pregnant (n=2586).
finding: Recently pregnant women exhibited significantly lower HbA1c levels and higher use of continuous subcutaneous insulin infusion and continuous glucose monitors compared to ever or never pregnant women, though adverse maternal and fetal outcomes remained high despite high technology uptake.
followup_time: Up to 1 year postpartum for a subset of 130 women; otherwise N/A as primarily a cross-sectional study
cross-section timing: Data for recently pregnant women collected between 2010 and 2013
